title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that evaluated whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—shared initial LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) + a deterministic Batfish‑style validator + at most one automated LLM repair—reduces deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures on intent→vendor‑CLI tasks. Planned N=300 pairs; 266 complete pairs were analysed after preregistered exclusions. Baseline pass-rate = 260/266 (97.744%); guarded (final GVR) pass-rate = 265/266 (99.624%). Paired difference = 0.01879699248; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. Paired bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Repair was invoked for 6 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not recorded in per‑task artifacts and thus could not be evaluated. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the observed absolute improvement is small and did not meet the preregistered α=0.05 decision rule. We present preregistered design details, deterministic validator semantics, complete numeric outcomes, representative artifact‑grounded repair examples, contamination findings (no exact public duplicates flagged), and an evidence‑grounded discussion of limitations and implications.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored for operational Network Operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→CLI translation and automated maintenance workflows [1], but their stochastic outputs can include syntactic and semantic errors (missing or misordered commands, unauthorized field touches, or sequence violations) that pose operational risk. To reduce that risk, recent prototype architectures interpose deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish or header‑space analyses) and bounded repair loops in generate–verify–repair (GVR) patterns so only outputs that pass an oracle are considered safe [2–4]. Prior works document components and prototypes but few preregistered, paired, artifact‑archived evaluations that quantify verifier‑triggered repair benefit on vendor‑specific CLI tasks.

Motivated by that gap we preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired design to answer: Does a GVR pipeline that uses (a) a single sampled initial LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate semantics), (b) a deterministic Batfish‑style validator, and (c) at most one automated LLM repair call reduce deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures compared to assessing the same initial candidate without repair? Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation that preserves the exact estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), reports full contingency counts and exact tests, and provides representative validator traces and repair examples for audit.
sections.related_work:
LLMs have been applied to NetOps and configuration synthesis in prototype systems and benchmarks that evaluate intent→CLI translation and configuration correctness [1]. Surveys of LLMs for network operations and AIOps summarize failure modes (hallucination, constraint violations) and advocate grounding and verification components when automating NetOps tasks [2]. Generate–verify–repair architectures have been proposed in code generation and regulated domains to provide deterministic validation by interposing oracles and bounded repair loops [3]. Network verification tools such as Batfish and header‑space analyses provide deterministic reachability, sequencing, and constraint checks and have been proposed as verifiers in LLM‑augmented NetOps pipelines [4]. Studies of LLM requirements for correct router configuration synthesis emphasize sequencing, dependency, and vendor‑dialect challenges that motivate verifier augmentation [5].

Our study differs by executing a preregistered paired test under shared_initial_candidate semantics, archiving raw model traces and validator outputs per episode, and reporting exact paired counts and the preregistered inferential result with diagnostic bootstrap intervals for effect‑magnitude assessment.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The experiment was preregistered as study cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same single sampled initial model candidate is used to compute both baseline and guarded outcomes; only validator‑triggered repair can change the guarded outcome). The preregistration specifies a confirmatory paired design with N=300 task pairs, two vendor clusters (150 Cisco‑like, 150 Juniper‑like), and exact inferential and missingness handling procedures.

Task bank and sampling: A deterministic synthetic task generator plus public NetConfEval‑style examples produced the task bank. Planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × 2 conditions). Deterministic generation seeds, the per‑task manifest, and reference answers are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and representative entries are present under execution/scoring/*.json. Inclusion and exclusion rules followed the preregistration; 34 both‑arm provider/infrastructure failures were excluded per the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule, leaving 266 complete paired units for primary analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model and orchestration: The declared model used in execution was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Archived model configuration fields include maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, max_output_tokens = 1024, provider = openai_responses, and temperature = null/unset. Provider call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 306 with 34 failed calls; stage accounting reports shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 6. These execution artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/execution_log.jsonl) are archived for reproducibility.

Deterministic validator semantics: The binary oracle used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. For each episode the validator performs CLI syntactic parsing/normalization, required‑sequence checks (expected_sequence vs parsed commands), allowed‑field/allowed‑touch checks, and reachability/constraint validation against the synthetic topology. Episode‑level validator traces archive parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation codes, and a normalized_configuration string (see execution/scoring/*.json for examples). The validator's binary pass/fail is the primary endpoint.

Repair loop and shared_initial_candidate mechanics: Per the preregistered adapter contract, a single initial sample is shared across baseline and guarded conditions (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). If the validator fails that candidate the guarded arm may invoke at most one automated LLM repair call. Repair prompts expose validator failure codes and task constraints and ask the LLM to produce a corrected configuration; repair provider traces are archived when invoked. The design choice of ≤1 repair was preregistered to represent a bounded automated correction before human escalation.

Analysis plan and inferential methods: The primary confirmatory test is the exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes (α=0.05). To report effect magnitude and uncertainty we preregistered a paired bootstrap percentile CI with B=10,000 resamples and seed=1729; the bootstrap CI provides an empirical view of paired‑difference variability even when discordant counts are small. This dual reporting follows the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. Secondary estimands included median_repair_iterations_per_task and median end‑to‑end latency (the latter could not be evaluated because per‑episode latency was not archived). Missingness handling followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (34 both‑arm provider failures excluded from primary test) with a sensitivity analysis that treats excluded episodes conservatively as failures.
sections.results:
Execution accounting: planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 532; failed episodes = 68. Model call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34 (deterministic_reconciliation.json). Repair stage calls recorded = 6. Complete paired units analysed = 266 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 266): baseline successes = 260; guarded final successes = 265. Paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 260 (both pass), n10 = 5 (guarded pass only), n01 = 0 (baseline pass only), n00 = 1 (both fail). Observed proportions: baseline = 260/266 = 0.9774436090; guarded = 265/266 = 0.9962406015. Paired difference = 0.01879699248.

Inferential results: exact McNemar two‑sided test (preregistered) yields p = 0.0625 (α=0.05 → preregistered decision: do not reject). Paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) for the paired difference = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records bootstrap parameters). The bootstrap CI narrowly excludes zero while the exact McNemar p does not, reflecting discreteness of exact McNemar in small‑discordant samples (n10 + n01 = 5).

Repair invocation and representative artifacts: Repair was invoked for 6 tasks (repair stage_count = 6); median repair iterations per task = 0. Representative failure and repair artifacts are archived: task-000008 illustrates a shared initial candidate that contained an incomplete final token (execution/responses/task-000008-shared-initial.txt) and an accepted corrected guarded configuration (execution/responses/task-000008-guarded.txt). Episode validator traces (execution/scoring/task-000008-*.json) include the validator failure codes and normalized_configuration that passed after repair. All raw responses, per‑episode validator traces, and provider call logs are archived in execution/ for audit.

Contamination and sensitivity: analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no exact-public-duplicate flags; therefore no task was excluded for exact public duplication. Sensitivity analysis treating the 34 excluded both‑arm episodes as failures (conservative N=300) yields baseline = 260/300 = 0.866667 and guarded = 265/300 = 0.883333 with the same discordant counts and exact McNemar p = 0.0625, indicating the primary inferential conclusion is robust to the preregistered conservative missingness treatment.

Operational metrics not evaluable: the preregistered latency estimand (median end‑to‑end latency ≤ 60 s) could not be evaluated because per‑episode timing was not present in the archived per‑task artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation: The guarded GVR pipeline produced a small absolute increase in validator pass‑rate (~1.88 percentage points). Under the preregistered exact McNemar decision rule this improvement did not reach α=0.05 (p=0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) narrowly excludes zero; we included the bootstrap CI alongside McNemar because McNemar depends only on discordant counts (discrete) and can yield conservative p‑values when discordant counts are small, whereas the bootstrap CI summarizes resampled paired‑difference variability and provides a continuous estimate of effect magnitude.

Operational implications and boundary conditions: Baseline first‑pass accuracy was high (~97.7%), leaving few failures that repair could correct; repair invocations were rare (6/300). For high first‑pass accuracy workloads the marginal operational benefit of adding a bounded automated repair stage may be limited. GVR may be more valuable for task sets or models with lower initial pass rates or when the verifier covers a broader set of semantic properties. Importantly, our estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics isolates the repair's contribution for a fixed initial draw and does not measure benefits that could accrue from alternative strategies (e.g., multiple independent draws or constrained first‑pass prompting).

Threats to validity: Internal validity — the shared_initial_candidate estimand measures only validator‑triggered repair effect for a fixed initial sample; it does not compare alternative generation strategies that were not preregistered or executed. Construct validity — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule set (syntax, required sequences, allowed touches, reachability) and cannot detect semantic errors outside its battery. External validity — tasks derive from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor clusters; results do not necessarily generalize to other vendors, larger production topologies, or different workload distributions. Conclusion validity — small discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0) and exclusion of 34 provider‑failure pairs reduced power and inferential precision.

Design lessons and reproducibility recommendations grounded in archived artifacts: (1) For high baseline accuracy cases, select task corpora with lower baseline pass rates or increase N to ensure informative discordant counts. (2) Archive per‑episode latency and pipeline timing to evaluate preregistered operational bounds (H2 latency could not be evaluated here). (3) Expand validator rule coverage and report validator test coverage metrics so construct validity of verification is measurable. (4) When shared_initial_candidate semantics are used, explicitly justify the choice in relation to the operational question; alternative paired arms (independent generation draws, constrained prompting) should be preregistered if they are of scientific interest.

Reproducibility: All relevant execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/execution_log.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, deterministic_reconciliation.json, and per‑episode scoring traces under execution/scoring/*.json. The paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor parameters (bootstrap B=10,000, seed=1729) and exact‑McNemar procedure were archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The study’s preregistration identifier and task manifests are archived for audit.
sections.conclusion:
A preregistered paired experiment evaluated a GVR pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + ≤1 automated repair) on intent→CLI tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Across 266 analysed pairs the guarded pipeline improved validator pass rate by 0.01879699248 but did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule (p=0.0625); a paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) narrowly excludes zero. Repair calls were rare (6/300) and median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not archived and could not be assessed. All execution and analysis artifacts, including raw responses, validator traces, provider call accounting, and reconciliation manifests, are archived in the evidence bundle to support reanalysis and follow‑on work.

References
[1] C. Wang, M. Scazzariello, A. Farshin, S. Ferlin, D. Kostić, and M. Chiesa, “NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration?,” Proc. ACM, 2024. doi:10.1145/3656296.
[2] S. Y. Long, J. Tan, B. Mao, F. Tang, Y. Li, M. Zhao, and N. Kato, “A Survey on Intelligent Network Operations and Performance Optimization Based on Large Language Models,” IEEE Commun. Surveys & Tutorials, 2025. doi:10.1109/comst.2025.3526606.
[3] R. Cadenas, “Convergent Correctness in Stochastic Code Generation: A Generate‑Verify‑Repair Architecture for Deterministic Validation of Autonomous AI Coding Agents in Regulated Environments,” SSRN, 2026. doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899.
[4] M. Brown, A. Fogel, D. Halperin, V. Heorhiadi, R. Mahajan, and T. Millstein, “Lessons from the evolution of the Batfish configuration analysis tool,” Proc., 2023. doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866.
[5] R. Mondal, A. Tang, R. Beckett, T. Millstein, and G. Varghese, “What do LLMs need to Synthesize Correct Router Configurations?,” Proc., 2023. doi:10.1145/3626111.3628194.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both arms used the same single sampled initial candidate per preregistration; the estimand measures validator‑triggered repair benefit for that fixed initial sample and does not evaluate independent first‑pass generations or constrained first‑pass prompting strategies.

Missingness and sample reduction: planned N=300 pairs; after infrastructure/provider exclusions 266 pairs were complete and 34 both‑arm episodes were excluded per preregistered rules, reducing effective sample size and precision.
Small discordant counts: primary inference used exact McNemar with few discordants (n10=5, n01=0); conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic/semantic/reachability rules; semantic violations outside its coverage are possible and unmeasured.

Runtime nondeterminism and sampling: archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null and no deterministic seed; nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for recorded model calls.
H2 latency not evaluated: per‑episode end‑to‑end latency was not present in archived per‑task artifacts and therefore the preregistered latency bound (median ≤ 60 s) could not be assessed.

External validity: task corpus derives from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal benefit across other vendors, larger topologies, or production deployments.
